description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and Accuracy, representing three distinct accuracy metrics. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence", utilizes a linear scale ranging from approximately 0.86 to 1.00, with angled numeric tick labels spaced predominantly at intervals of 0.01 from 0.88 to 1.00, alongside an initial label at 0.86. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy", employs a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with numeric tick labels evenly spaced at intervals of 0.2. All data points across the three series include vertical error bars. The "Final Accuracy" line is plotted in blue with open circle markers and a solid line style. It maintains a relatively high and stable trend, beginning at approximately 0.93 at x=0.86, dipping slightly to roughly 0.96 at x=0.90 and x=0.93, peaking near 1.00 at x=0.97 and x=0.99, and ending at about 0.98 at x=1.00. The "Δ Accuracy" line is depicted in orange with open diamond markers and a dashed line style. It begins at approximately 0.29 at x=0.86, declines to roughly 0.13 at x=0.91, rises to a minor peak of about 0.21 at x=0.92, drops to a low of approximately 0.05 at x=0.95, and eventually rises to end at roughly 0.21 at x=1.00. The "Initial Accuracy" line is shown in green with open square markers and a dash-dot line style. It starts at approximately 0.64 at x=0.86, increases to roughly 0.84 at x=0.91, dips to about 0.76 at x=0.92, rises to peak values of approximately 0.93 at x=0.95 and x=0.99, and finally declines to end at approximately 0.77 at x=1.00.
